prae-mētor , ātus, 1,
I.v. dep. a., to measure or measure out beforehand (post-class.), Sol. 40 (dub.; al. metatum).—Hence, in pass. signif.: praemētātus , a, um, measured or meted out beforehand: “praemetata divūm itinera,” predestined, Mart. Cap. 8, § 811 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
